Messages.Author: Richter
Messages.Body:
Hi all,

My fellow priscus Blackwood from Sabbat In France just write us about
an idea to manage the third round lose-deal problem and the tie break
at the same time.

In case of a tie for Final (equal GW, VP and TP), we can compare in
this order :
- VP made in third round,
- VP made in second round,
- VP made in first round.

This gives a little boost to the 3rd round but imho in a good way for
balancing the cheesy lose-deal problem.

bye,

Richter,
!Brujah priscus
http://sabbatinfrance.org

Not bad.

Note that comparing VP in the first round is superfluous -- if you're tied in
overall VPs and tied in 3rd round VPs and tied in 2nd round VPs, it follows that
you're tied in first round VPs.

Slightly better, IMO, would be:
GW in the third round
GW in the second round
VP in the third round
VP in the second round

Frederick Scott a écrit :

Player already having like 1GW+4VP before entering 3rd round and having
experience of tournaments of 25ish players knows that 2VP will ensure
him a place in final round at 99%.
So he will quickly lose-deal in third round to grab his 2VPs, often
ruining the game by not playing to win (and this is HARD to detect and
sanction as a good player may put himself in shit to get "the right"
to lose deal).

It is more obvious know with 2-days continental tournaments when there
is 40 seats in day two for 60 players in day one. In this case, 2VPs
are huge in 3rd round even if you do not have any GW.

Richter

OK, I thought it was something like that. But this strikes as being
totally negligible - if not entirely useless - in combating the
effect. If a player has, for whatever reason, abandoned his motivation
towards going for a game win in the third round, I don't see upweighting
the third round GWs and VPs as making a difference. In fact, in the
situation above, it may even increase his incentive to make the lose
deal, since the VPs gained in the third round are more likely to get
him over the top and into the final. On the other hand, if he's
already reasoned that it's better to sacrifice his ability to grab a GW
in the last round (which is good for a higher preliminary round ranking)
in favor of the more certain route to making the finals at all, increasing
the value of the game win isn't going to affect that reasoning as far
as I can see.

Fred

So what? That doesn't mean anything to the guy in this position.
I understood that we were only talking about a tie break after tournament
points are considered, or in place of tournament points. So for someone
who feels he just needs more victory points to buttress a single game
win (or however many game wins he feels is enough), he doesn't care
about a tie break further down the line. Just getting victory points
is what's important. And if they're "superior" victory points, so much
the better. But he doesn't care about a "superior" game win if it
jeopardizes a higher value tie break - raw number of victory points.
And you must assume he sees it that way to have conjectured that problem
in the first place.

> > On the other hand, if he's
> > already reasoned that it's better to sacrifice his ability to grab a GW
> > in the last round (which is good for a higher preliminary round ranking)

> But it solves some tie problems and goes into the right direction.
> Anyway the third round can not be given an unbalancing value.

More so than being "not perfect", it accomplishes nothing of value vis-a-vis
the game-lose deal problem as you claimed. I suppose it doesn't hurt
anything in that it's something you can stick in front of a coin flip/
randomization tie break. I'm just saying that it doesn't solve any long-
standing problems having to do with players playing their final games
with an "outside" motivation to make the finals instead of playing to win.

> What do you propose ?

I propose nothing. I never claimed to have a solution to that sort of
problem.

Fred

Messages.Author: gpett...@gmail.com
Messages.Body:
Fred's right, we need to reward Third Round GWs but not Third Round
VPs; we need to go "around the bend":

In order of Precedence:
1. Total GWs
2. Total VPs
3. 3rd round GWs
4. 2nd round GWs
5. 1st round VPs
6. 2nd round VPs
7. TPs? Coin Toss?

This discourages losing deals in the third round without relegating the
first round to second-class status.



Messages.Author: preac...@gmx.at
Messages.Body:
LSJ schrieb:



I think there is a solution which has the advantage that it would be
more incentive to make winning-deals instead of loosing-deals:

Players are ranked according to:

1. GWs
2. VPs made in a game where also the GW was achieved ("VPs within the
GW") by the player
3. VPs made in a game where no GW was achieved by the player
4. TPs

There would be lesser incentive to make loosing-deals, as VPs made with
a GW have the higher priority. Also, this solution doesnt put emphasis
on any single round, all rounds would count the same.

How would this solution affect rankings and deals?
Would this be feasible?

Carl

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
"Richter" <denis....@metaboli.fr> wrote in message

news:1163071293.4...@m73g2000cwd.googlegroups.com...

> @Fred : I know this is not a major threat for 3rd round losedealers,
> but it will screw some of them from time to time and will make the
> losedeal technique a little less effective. And, as you said, it does
> not hurting anything, so why shouldn't we try ?

Perhaps adding complexity to tournament rules for no good reason might
be bad. However, in the case of tournament tie-breakers to stick in front
of the randomness method, I'm not sure a little extra complexity matters
one way or the other. So I'm really not opposed to using the idea
I'm just opposed to considering it to be any kind of solution to lose
deals. If judges started to think it was, it might become an "attractive
nuisance".

> We can also add some other little incentive features to the 3rd round
> like the finalists choosing their seating depending on their results in
> the 3rd round (on-fire player gets the best).

I doubt that would help, either. Remember, you're talking about
motivating a person who feels he has enough game wins to make the finals
if he can just find the most certain way of gaining one or two more
victory points. If he were worried about seating position in the finals,
he'd be going for the game win anyway.

It's actually a pretty thorny problem, IMO.

Fred
